title: Disagreement on a three-coordinate hard input
statement: Choose $i\\in\\{0,1,2\\}$ and a map $j:\\{-1,1\\}\\to\\{0,1,2\\}$ such that $j(a)\\ne i$ for both signs $a$. Choose a sign $s$ and an index $r\\in\\{0,1,2\\}$ independently and uniformly, and form the three-coordinate sign vector whose coordinate $r$ is $-s$ and whose other coordinates are $s$. The probability that this vector differs from the vector obtained by applying the same construction with sign equal to its $i$th coordinate and index $j$ of that coordinate is $2/3$.
